Inside

What's inside

The room, wall to wall.

One long bar, a carved sign, a pool room with its own door, a patio under the string lights, and a back lounge that says it out loud: we ♥ Buckley.

On tap

Manny's, Elysian, Deschutes Fresh Squeezed, Angry Orchard — and a Bud Light for the game. The handles rotate; the carved sign above them doesn't.

The back bar

The kitchen

Pizza in 7" and 16" (gluten-free on a 10"), burgers with a peanut-butter one the regulars swear by, baskets, and the Firehouse Frenzy for the table.

Dine in · take out · delivery

The pool room

Added in the 2018 remodel with its own door — so the game in there doesn't fight the game on the screens out here.

Through the side door

The patio

Iron tables under red umbrellas and string lights, off the sidewalk on Main — the outdoor-seating that eight different Google reviews bothered to mention.

Out front, in season

The screens

Seahawks Sundays are the house religion — regulars have their stools and the staff knows which ones. Pull tabs at the bar.

Every wall

The back lounge

Couches under a wall of Rainier posters and a WE ♥ BUCKLEY sign. Where the group ends up after the second pitcher.

The story

The story

Boyle's Tavern. Logger's Inn. Firehouse.

This corner of Main Street has poured drinks for Buckley under three names. The Firehouse chapter started in November 2000, when two Microsoft guys cashed in enough stock options to buy the old Logger's Inn — a place where, as the Courier-Herald put it, "the floor was so rotten a refrigerator was falling through it." They rebuilt it as a pizza pub, and in short order it was the busiest room in downtown Buckley.

Marnie Hayes took the keys in 2010. In 2017 she bought the old D'Jon's building a few doors down, stripped it to three walls, added the pool room and the patio — and had the early-1900s bar top carried down the sidewalk by hand. The new Firehouse opened in time for the Log Show, and it's been the official after-party ever since.

The walls carry the rest: old photographs, antique logging saws, and booths from Wilkeson's original Pick & Shovel. "The people who come in and out of this place," Marnie says, "are genuinely some of the nicest people in the world."

Questions

Got questions?

Before you come in.

Do you take reservations?
No — it's first come, first stool. Big group? Call ahead at (360) 829-2999 and we'll tell you how the room looks.
Can I get it to go?
Yes — takeout at the bar, or delivery through DoorDash. The one exception is the weekly specials and the $7.95 lunch deals: those are in-house only.
Cash or card?
Both. We take credit and debit, and we give 4% off when you pay cash.
Gluten-free?
Any pizza can be made gluten-free on a 10" crust for the price of a 16".
Is this really the Log Show after-party?
The official one. Every June when the parade comes down Main Street, it ends here — the staff shirts say so.
Where do I park?
Street parking on Main and the side streets. Thursdays the curb out front fills with motorcycles — that's bike night, not a sign we're closed.

The game's on. The stool's open.
